subject.title: feat: add jsonl support to memory indexer

question: Should builtin Memory Core accept arbitrary JSONL extra paths, and if so which JSON fields and privacy rules define the safe searchable-text projection?
rationale: The repository already supports OpenClaw-managed session JSONL through a dedicated sanitized source, but arbitrary hook logs have no documented schema or privacy contract. Code can implement either direction, but it cannot safely choose what raw structured data becomes embeddable.

options.title: Define a bounded builtin JSONL contract
options.body: Approve JSONL only through an explicit text-field projection and line-mapped parser in Memory Core, with privacy limits and end-to-end retrieval support.

options.title: Keep arbitrary JSONL external
options.body: Document session-memory, QMD, or a converter/plugin workflow for raw logs and retain Markdown-oriented `extraPaths` as the builtin contract.

recommendation.title: Define a bounded builtin JSONL contract
recommendation.body: Approve JSONL only through an explicit text-field projection and line-mapped parser in Memory Core, with privacy limits and end-to-end retrieval support.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent involvement spans the current Memory Core admission, indexing, retrieval, and session-JSONL paths, making this the strongest available routing signal.
